principle: Do not copy or merge subsystems until their trust, persistence, lifecycle and failure semantics have an explicit adapter contract and cross-repository tests.

properties: durable membership and revocation lookup for federation admission

component_map.reason: This is an agent-key registry keyed by agent_id, not a user/tenant principal identity registry. It provides durable membership and revocation checks for executable agents only.

properties: trusted callback under SQLite write transaction
protected API remains disabled until a resolver is configured

component_map.reason: A durable principal trust store now exists in the primary repository. External identity-provider enrollment, gateway authentication binding and production provisioning controls remain open.
Secondary local software attestation proves possession of a locally derived key; it is not external hardware attestation or a trusted principal identity.
The schemas, ownership rules and rollback guarantees differ; the secondary journal advertises a local hash chain without an external monotonic anchor.
The runtimes expose different execution contracts and have distinct lifecycle and state ownership.
No matching offline authorization snapshot or durable outbox contract is present in the assessed secondary branch.
component_map.candidate: PR #117 proposes Ed25519 issuer-authenticated snapshots; not yet part of the assessed primary base ref.

properties: service graph with a CONSENSUS role

component_map.reason: A topology role named CONSENSUS is not a consensus algorithm; secondary runtime explicitly rejects consensus opt-in.
These capabilities are candidates for isolated adapters, not replacements for primary trust, audit or authorization controls.

properties: protected operations return 503 until authentication is configured

component_map.reason: The secondary API is intentionally closed without a configured principal resolver; it must remain closed until a real trust adapter exists.

requirements: distinct principal IDs and agent IDs; never infer one from the other
authenticated principal-to-public-key or trusted external identity binding
durable revocation tombstones and restart-safe lookup
issuer and principal status checked at execution admission
no authorization based on bootstrap client labels or caller-supplied identity strings
no implicit trust from local PUF or self-attestation

integration_gates: Bind the principal registry to a trusted enrollment/authentication provider and to the federation verifier; keep ingress disabled until this wiring is tested.
Define versioned shared contracts without importing either runtime into the other.
Implement one-way adapters first; prohibit implicit cross-runtime authority escalation.
Verify signed envelope, key revocation, replay, principal isolation and audit attribution in cross-repository tests.
Test partial outages, stale epochs, duplicate delivery and restart recovery.
Only then consider a bidirectional runtime bridge.
non_goals: No merge of the two repositories.
No replacement of the primary runtime by the secondary IntegratedRuntime.
No claim that simulated PUF is hardware attestation.
No claim that MIAM topology supplies distributed consensus.
No sharing of private keys or raw memory databases.
No assumption that the primary SQLite agent registry authenticates human principals.
